description: Use this to read or quote an EU legislative provision, such as PSD2 Article 97 or RTS-SCA Article 5. Returns the source text of an article, annex or recital as markdown, with its cite anchor, provenance and text state; a long provision paginates by structural block. version_id is optional, and a pinned version id is refused with the URL where that text is published. include_correspondences adds the cross-instrument article equivalences.

cursor.description: Continue a paginated provision. Bound to the release.

include_correspondences.description: Off by default. When true, an article carries correspondences[]: the cross-instrument article equivalences the corpus publishes, each with the counterpart's own get_provision locator, version and cite anchor. null means the release predates the mapping table, not that the article has none.

instrument_id.description: Registry id of the instrument, e.g. "psd-2".

annex.description: Annex number, roman or arabic ("I", "1"); omit for an instrument whose single annex is unnumbered.

kind.description: Which kind of provision the locator names.

paragraph.description: Numbered paragraph within the article, e.g. "2".

point.description: Lettered point within the paragraph, e.g. "b".

on_date.description: ISO date; returns the provision-level applicability view.

version_id.description: Omit, or pass "current", for the served text. A pinned version id returns version_not_served with the URL where that text is published.

name: get_provision

paragraph_pairs.description: A paragraph-specific mapping's verified rows, as {predecessor, successor} provision labels ("5(3)", "36(4)"); absent where the mapping is article to article; a side without a paragraph number is a printed pairing that fell back to its article. Correspondences are recorded on the article; where the correlation table is paragraph-specific and the pairing is verified by wording, an entry carries `paragraph_pairs`. A request narrowed to a paragraph or a point still receives the whole article's mappings, and a warning says whether any entry is paragraph-level.

relationship.description: amended_from or supersedes, the analysis layer's own vocabulary, or their mechanical inverses amended_into and superseded_by.

annex.description: Annex number, roman or arabic ("I", "1"); omit for an instrument whose single annex is unnumbered.

kind.description: Which kind of provision the locator names.

paragraph.description: Numbered paragraph within the article, e.g. "2".

point.description: Lettered point within the paragraph, e.g. "b".

correspondences.description: An annex or a recital carries an empty list. A mapping this service will not serve is omitted and correspondence_withheld names the instrument and the reason, so a short list is never silently under-claimed.

follows_part.description: The bar follows the closing subparagraph of the paragraph in `follows`.

precedes_part.description: The bar precedes the closing subparagraph of the paragraph in `precedes`.

deletions.description: Deletions marked on the whole provision, in source order. A EUR-Lex deletion stub names the act that deleted what stood there: "within": the nth "—————" in the provision text; "after": something deleted after this provision (a whole article or chapter), with `heading` naming the Title, Chapter or Section heading it stands under when one comes between them; "title": in its heading. A record with source "council_compromise" is a ▌ the Council compromise text prints on a line of its own where it deleted a point, paragraph or passage: `follows` and `precedes` name the items it stands between ("after": at the end of the provision text, precedes null, with `heading` as for a stub), `follows_part` or `precedes_part` says that side is the paragraph's closing subparagraph; `page` and `source_url` give the page of the Council document that prints it; the provision text carries no mark for it. The record says where the bar stands, not what was removed, and compare_versions does not show it. Mechanically derived from the source; not part of the legal text. Null means no record is served for this provision (see the typed warning), never that nothing was deleted.

markdown.description: The provision's source text as markdown. A sub- or superscript with no Unicode form is inline <sub>/<sup> (K<sub>IRB</sub>); one with a Unicode form uses it (m²).

complete.description: All notes referenced in this response's text, not the whole document or later pages.

source_notes.description: Null means unverified/unsupported coverage or an older release; consult the typed warning. Not an empty note inventory. Legal content_hash and block counts exclude this attachment. The verified note scope is DMD articles and recitals. Introductory citations are not an MCP provision kind: their notes remain on the website and exports, not attached to articles.

title.description: Plain text: a script with a Unicode form uses it, one without reads flat (KCCP).

title_path.description: Plain text: a script with a Unicode form uses it, one without reads flat (KCCP).

title: Read EU legislative provision
